items.title: AG-C: Nicky Liow paid RM10m compound before money laundering charges withdrawn
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Nicky Liow Soon Hee paid a RM10 million compound in 2023 before the Attorney General's Chambers (A-GC) withdrew 26 money laundering charges against him. "After reviewing the representations and the available evidence, the A-GC agreed to offer a RM10 million compound, which Liow agreed and paid on May 29, 2023. "Following payment of the compound, the prosecution withdrew all 26 charges against Liow in accordance with Section 92.

items.title: Three held over syndicate creating fake passport movement records for RM700
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has crippled a "flying passport" syndicate that allegedly created fake movement records by processing foreign passports without their owners being present at entry points. Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said three suspects, aged between 33 and 41, were arrested yesterday in a special operation at Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB), Gelang Patah, Johor. Zakaria said the syndicate charged RM700 for each foreign passport processed through the illegal service.

items.title: Tropicana builds Langkawi portfolio with six projects, taps foreign demand
items.summary: LANGKAWI: Tropicana Corp Bhd is building up in Langkawi, Kedah, with six development projects backed by a land bank spanning about 730 hectares, positioning the property developer to tap into growing demand for resort-style living, hospitality and tourism-led real estate on the island. At the centre of its Langkawi expansion is Tropicana Cenang, a 2.14ha freehold beachfront integrated development in Pantai Cenang comprising serviced residences, retail outlets and hospitality components. The development has gained strong market traction, with its first two phases, Assana Serviced Suites and Merissa Serviced Suites, fully sold.

items.title: Rising costs top Singapore businesses' concerns, survey finds
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Rising business costs have become the biggest concern for Singapore companies as geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainty weigh on sentiment, a survey by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry has shown, reported Xinhua. According to the survey released on Wednesday, the most commonly cited concern was rising business costs, selected by 71.8 per cent of respondents. Thirty-eight per cent of respondents were neutral on business prospects, while 34 per cent were pessimistic and only 20 per cent were optimistic.

items.title: Gold heads for best week since January; US jobs data in focus
items.summary: Spot gold was up 0.6 per cent at US$4,262.39 per ounce, as of 0421 GMT after hitting a seven-week high on Thursday. US gold futures gained 0.5 per cent to US$4,321.50. Spot silver added 1.3 per cent to US$62.27, platinum rose 0.5 per cent to US$1,737.25, while palladium dropped 0.2 per cent to US$1,368.37.

items.title: Nurul Izzah's resignation reflects PKR turmoil, says Pas
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas believes Nurul Izzah Anwar's resignation as PKR deputy president reflects serious internal problems within the ruling party. Its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the deputy president's role was crucial, particularly when the party president was occupied with his duties as prime minister. "When a deputy president resigns, it will certainly have an impact on the party.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia stays lower at midday amid mixed regional markets
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Public Bank dropped eight sen to RM10.72 and RM5.15, respectively, CIMB Group lost six sen to RM7.91, and IHH Healthcare eased two sen to RM8.31, while Public Bank added six sen to RM14.54. Of the active stocks, Perak Transit gained four sen to 21.5 sen, YTL Corp climbed 16 sen to RM2.13, and YTL Power International was 29 sen stronger at RM4.66, while Malaysian Resources Corp and HHRG were flat at 34 sen and 10.5 sen, respectively. As for the top losers, Batu Kawan slumped 66 sen to RM20.74, Malaysian Pacific Industries shed 42 sen to RM47.24, United Plantations fell 32 sen to RM33.88, and UMS Integration slid 19 sen to RM7.56.

items.title: Singapore banks ride Asia's wealth boom to weather rates headwind
items.summary: SINGAPORE: A surge in income from wealth management and other fee revenue helped Singapore's top three banks to cushion the impact of low interest rates, as lenders bet the region's fast-growing affluent population will continue to underpin growth this year. OCBC, Singapore's second-largest bank, said on Friday its April-June net profit jumped 22 per cent to S$2.22 billion (US$1.73 billion), well above estimates, while UOB's net profit was up 10 per cent to S$1.5 billion, beating forecasts. The benchmark stock index rose 0.7 per cent.

items.title: Hadi says Bersatu out of PN after Muhyiddin announced new coalition
items.summary: MARANG: Bersatu's membership in Perikatan Nasional has been automatically revoked following its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's announcement that the party would form a new coalition. Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said this was in line with the coalition's constitution. Last month, Muhyiddin, who is Pagoh member of parliament, reportedly said Bersatu would form a new coalition with several other parties after the Negri Sembilan state election.

items.title: Elderly couple's 30-year drug use ends in nationwide bust
items.summary: KUANTAN: An elderly married couple were among 1,209 people who tested positive for drugs during a three-day nationwide operation by the National Anti-Drug Agency. He said 1,606 people were arrested during the operation, which ended yesterday, with 1,209 of them, including 56 women, testing positive for drugs. On the operation in Pahang, Mahadzir said 131 of the 254 arrested were newly detected addicts.

items.title: PH studying election setbacks as sentiment overtakes performance - Mustapha
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Public sentiment, rather than government performance, is now playing a bigger role in shaping voters' decisions, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. Mustapha, who is also Sabah Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the coalition had begun analysing the outcomes of the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections. However, I believe we still have time to address our weaknesses," he said when asked whether the two state election results would affect PH's preparations for upcoming elections.

items.title: Kuching, Samarahan record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Kuching and Samarahan recorded unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) on Friday morning. According to data from the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), as of 10am, Kuching recorded an API reading of 133, while Samarahan recorded 135. Other districts in Sarawak recorded moderate readings, including Sarikei at 90, Sri Aman and Sibu at 86, Bintulu at 83, Mukah at 76 and Samalaju at 75.

items.title: Man trapped, another injured after pickup truck collides with cement lorry
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (operations) Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.04am reporting the crash at KM397.1 of the southbound carriageway. He said five firefighters from the Bukit Sentosa Fire and Rescue Station, along with a light fire rescue tender, were deployed to the scene. Ashrul said firefighters immediately began extrication operations to free the trapped victim, while the injured man received medical assistance.

items.title: Taxi drivers can opt for non-S70 models under Teksi Madani
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Taxi drivers are allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70 under the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme (Teksi Madani). "Taxi drivers are encouraged to switch to Teksi Madani to enjoy the various incentives offered. "However, to assist applicants who already have existing vehicles or were unsuccessful in obtaining approval for hire-purchase financing under the Teksi Madani programme, applicants are still allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70," Apad said in a statement today.

items.title: Married couple among three charged over false Perkeso claims
items.summary: The accused — M. S. Gunaseelan, 45, his wife S. Theen Malar, 45, and A. S. Shisman, 45 — entered their pleas after the charges were read before judge Shahrul Rizal Majid. He was charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act, punishable under Section 24(2) of the same act. Theen Malar and Shisman were charged under Section 28(1)(c), read together with Section 18 of the same act, punishable under Section 24(2), for abetting the offence.

items.title: Hadi says Bersatu no longer part of Perikatan after plans for new coalition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is no longer a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Abdul Hadi said the PN constitution provides that any party choosing to join or establish another alliance would automatically cease to be a member of the coalition. “They (Bersatu) have already stated their intention to want to form another ‘team’.

items.title: ‘No more warnings’: Immigration D-G vows action against rogue officers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department will not protect any of its officers and personnel involved in misconduct, including corruption or abuse of power, and immediate stern action will instead be taken against them without compromise. We will take immediate action (against officers involved in misconduct),” he said in his speech at the department’s monthly assembly here today. Citing the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) involving the PLKS application and approval process, Zakaria said the department had received initial information on the involvement of its officers and personnel in the case.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz calls on Negri exco members to discharge duties with honesty, fairness
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded the state's new executive councillors (Exco) to carry out the trust placed in them and their responsibilities with honesty, fairness and professionalism. Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. Tuanku Muhriz said the appointments represented a challenge for all the Exco members, who also serve as state assemblymen for their respective constituencies.

items.title: Taxi drivers can replace vehicles with models other than Proton S70, says APAD
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Taxi drivers are allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70 under the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme (Teksi Madani). This applies although the Transport Ministry’s policy announced on April 23 stipulated that new applications or taxi replacements under the programme would be voluntary and limited to the purchase of the Proton S70 taxi package offered under the programme. “Taxi drivers are encouraged to switch to Teksi Madani to enjoy the various incentives offered.

items.title: [UPDATED] Ismail Sabri determined to clear name despite health setback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob remains determined to clear his name as he prepares to face charges under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act later this month. His lawyer, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, who visited the Bera member of parliament shortly after the court adjourned the charging proceedings, said he had updated Ismail Sabri on the day's developments. Ismail Sabri, 66, is scheduled to undergo a pacemaker procedure at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this afternoon due to an irregular heartbeat.

items.title: Two dead, including gunman, at school shooting in Thailand, officials say
items.summary: BANG KRUAI: At least one teacher was killed and four other people injured by a student who opened fire at a school in Thailand north of Bangkok on Friday before killing himself, authorities said. Lt Col Dechrapee Kongdee, Nonthaburi police chief, confirmed the casualties to Reuters and said the suspected gunman had committed suicide. Among those injured were one teacher and three students, he said.

items.title: Tackling stray dog menace with registration, microchipping
items.summary: LETTERS: The growing number of stray dog incidents has become a serious public safety concern, with residents across the country reporting encounters in housing areas, near schools, playgrounds, markets and public parks. In Selangor, local authorities received 10,333 complaints related to stray dogs in 2025. In addition, 270 cases (75 per cent) involved owned pet dogs, while 90 cases (25 per cent) involved stray dogs, showing that irresponsible ownership is also a major contributor to public safety risks.

items.title: Police recover RM96k worth of stolen cattle, arrest 10
items.summary: Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the arrests enabled police to solve 20 cattle theft cases in the state. He said the operations involved four officers and 15 personnel from the Kelantan Criminal Investigation Department and the Pasir Puteh district police headquarters. "Police raided three locations in Bachok, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Terengganu.

items.title: Technician pleads not guilty to seven counts of sexually assaulting 14-year-old stepdaughter
items.summary: IPOH, August 7 — A technician was charged in the Sessions Court here today with seven counts of sexually assaulting his 14-year-old stepdaughter for the past three years in Bandar Universiti, Seri Iskandar. He was also charged with committing similar offences against the same victim in May 2024 and May 2025 at the same location. Nor Arfahanim urged the court to deny bail, arguing that the accused posed a risk of interfering with the victims and prosecution witnesses.

items.title: PN will not interfere in Bersatu Terengganu's internal affairs, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional will not interfere in Bersatu's internal affairs following the resignation of three senior Terengganu Bersatu leaders from their party positions. PN deputy chairman and Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said PN, particularly Pas, took note of the decision as it involved elected assemblymen who remained part of the Terengganu government. Tuan Ibrahim was commenting on Terengganu Bersatu chairman Datuk Razali Idris' decision to resign from his party post .

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in Jakarta was not flying aircraft, says Malaysia Aviation Group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has clarified that the Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in a recent incident was not operating the aircraft, saying flight safety was not compromised. MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said operational safety and crew fitness for duty remained non-negotiable at the group. MAG said it had commenced the first phase of mandatory drug screening for all pilots across its airlines, beginning with all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots.

items.title: Final beach trips become family's last memories of electrocuted policeman
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A policeman who was electrocuted while harvesting coconuts in Sabah had unknowingly spent his final days creating cherished memories with his family. Lance Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Rahim, 29, had taken his wife and their 2-year-old son to the beach several days in a row despite being exhausted from work, said his mother-in-law, Norizan Hamat. Norizan said Hafiz had made it a habit to video call the family daily and send photos of himself, his wife, Fatimah Syaera Zahrul Saharudin, 28, and their son, Hariz Idraqi, during their recent outings.

items.title: MACC-Customs anti-smuggling task force still under discussion, says department
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — The proposed joint task force between the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to combat smuggling and revenue leakages has yet to be finalised, with discussions between both agencies still ongoing. In a response to Malay Mail the Customs Department said the proposed collaboration remained at the discussion stage and further details would be announced once both parties reached an agreement. C4 Centre head of research and policy advocacy Arief Hamzan said while the proposed task force was a positive step towards addressing enforcement weaknesses, its role, powers and implementation mechanisms must be clearly defined.

items.title: Asian shares pause for US jobs, oil extends gains on Middle East risk
items.summary: Japan's Nikkei dropped 0.9 per cent although it was set for a weekly rise of 1.2 per cent. South Korea's KOSPI slipped 0.5 per cent and was down 5.0 per cent for the week for a seventh straight week of declines. China's CSI 300 rose 0.2 per cent.

items.title: MCMC: Under-16 social media restrictions aim to ensure greater platform accountability
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Aug 7 — Malaysia’s regulatory approach to restricting social media access for users under 16 underscores the need for platforms to practice higher levels of accountability in ensuring a safe online environment, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said. She said platform providers, as the developers and providers of social media products, should determine the safety features within the online environment. On June 1, Malaysia began enforcing its under-16 social media safeguards, requiring social media platforms to implement measures aimed at strengthening online safety and protecting young users.

items.title: Oil extends gains and stocks fall on fresh Hormuz worries
items.summary: HONG KONG: Oil prices extended gains and stocks fell further on Friday amid fading optimism over a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, as reports said Iran was planning to block US and Israeli ships from the waterway as part of a deal with Oman. Markets had enjoyed a healthy run-up at the start of the week as US President Donald Trump called off strikes on the Islamic republic and said an agreement was close, even though Tehran denied talks had taken place. Crude prices had begun edging up Wednesday and rallied as much as four per cent Thursday as the Fars news agency said Iran would look to prevent US and Israeli vessels from using the strait in any deal with Oman.

items.title: Guan Eng questions Umno's commitment to Penang unity govt after Reezal's remarks
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Lim Guan Eng today criticised Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican's remarks on Umno-DAP ties in Penang, questioning whether Umno remains committed to maintaining trust within the state's unity government. "By accusing DAP and PKR of engaging in identity politics, when it is BN and PN that are the real culprits, Reezal has launched an unwarranted attack on his supposed partners in the Penang state government," Lim said in a Facebook post today. Lim questioned whether ties between Umno and DAP in the Penang government could remain cordial and free of tension if Umno became the "enemy within" by making such remarks.

items.title: 10 assemblymen take oath as Negri Sembilan exco members
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Ten Negri Sembilan State Executive Council (exco) members were appointed today, with two retaining their positions and eight new faces joining the state administration. The two assemblymen retained in the exco line-up are Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Palong assemblyman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor. The eight new exco members are Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Chennah assemblyman Siow Kong Choon, Labu assemblywoman Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Sungai Lui assemblyman Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Gemencheh assemblyman Suhaimizan Bizar, Serting assemblyman Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah.

items.title: Police seek man accused of flashing, trying to abduct 13-year-old
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Police are tracking down a man to assist investigations into the alleged sexual harassment and attempted abduction of a 13-year-old schoolgirl in Taman Sri Saujana here. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said a report on the incident was lodged last Thursday. "Police are looking for a suspect described as a tall, thin and dark-complexioned man," he said when contacted yesterday.

items.title: Ten assemblymen sworn in as N. Sembilan exco members
items.summary: Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Palong assemblyman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor were retained as Exco members. The new appointees are Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Chennah assemblyman Siow Kong Choon, Labu assemblywoman Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Sungai Lui assemblyman Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Gemencheh assemblyman Suhaimizan Bizar, Serting assemblyman Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah. Also present at the swearing-in ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: [UPDATED] Mandatory drug tests for Malaysia Airlines pilots
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has introduced mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots following the arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia over alleged drug smuggling. The group said the screening exercise covers all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots and is expected to be completed by Aug 15. It said mandatory drug screening would subsequently be expanded to active cabin crew.

items.title: Saifuddin orders immediate probe after 3 cops electrocuted
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A comprehensive and transparent investigation has been ordered immediately to determine the actual cause of the electric shock tragedy that claimed the lives of three policemen in Beaufort yesterday. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that any weaknesses identified must be addressed immediately, while improvements must also be implemented to ensure that a similar incident does not recur. He also expessed his condolences to the families of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee and Corporal Chiu Teck Siong.

items.title: Indonesia's forex reserves fall to US$145.3bil in July
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves fell by around US$250 million in July to stand at US$145.34 billion at the end of that month, the central bank said on Friday, a level it said was above international standards and adequate to support external resilience. The change in the reserves reflected foreign revenue receipts, proceeds from the government's foreign currency bond sale, as well as payments of offshore public debt and the central bank's currency interventions to shore up the rupiah, Bank Indonesia said. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Trump signs executive order to impose 15pct tariff on polysilicon imports
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order imposing minimum import prices and a 15 per cent tariff on products made from polysilicon, a key material for solar panels and semiconductors, reported Xinhua. The minimum import prices will be set at US$21 per kilogram for polysilicon and US$100 per kilogram for polysilicon ingots and wafers, according to a White House proclamation. Trump also directed the US Commerce Department to establish a programme to encourage investment in domestic production of raw polysilicon and related downstream products.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz reminds new N. Sembilan exco to reject abuse of power, prioritise people
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded the state’s new executive councillors (Exco) to carry out the trust placed on them and their responsibilities with honesty, fairness and professionalism. Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. Tuanku Muhriz said the appointments represented a challenge for all the Exco members, who also serve as state assemblymen for their respective constituencies.

items.title: Terengganu technician loses RM58,500 in scam promising Indonesia export approval
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 7 — A women technician lost RM58,500 after falling victim to a scam offering to obtain a Food and Drug Administration (BPOM) certificate for the purpose of exporting products to Indonesia. Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said on March 23, 2024, the 38-year-old victim saw an advertisement related to Jom Eksport Ke Indonesia on Wan Muhd Ali’s Facebook social page. For Malaysian companies wishing to export food or health products to Indonesia, BPOM registration or approval is usually required depending on the type of product,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Kluang college student charged with murdering newborn girl
items.summary: KLUANG, Aug 7 — A college student was accused in the Magistrate’s Court here today on a charge of killing her newborn baby girl at a house here last week. Nurshazwen Mohd Idris, 19, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Nurasidah A. Rahman. According to the charge, Nurshazwen is charged with killing the baby girl she gave birth to at a house at Jalan Setia Mutiara 2/6, Taman Setia Mutiara here at about 10am, July 29.

items.title: Malaysia Aviation Group mandates pilot drug tests after off-duty crew member’s Jakarta drug arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has commenced mandatory drug screening for all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots and will implement stricter screening for all active pilots, going beyond current industry practice. The parent company of Malaysia Airlines Bhd has begun screening pilots across its airlines, with the exercise expected to be completed by August 15, 2026. In addition, MAG said the group will implement mandatory drug screening for all active pilots, complementing its existing random testing programme and will subsequently be expanded to active cabin crew.

items.title: Perak authorities probe suspected Irrawaddy dolphin carcass washed ashore in Ban Pecah
items.summary: Its director, Mohd Ghazali A. Manap, said it had yet to receive any official complaint regarding the discovery of the marine mammal, and only became aware of the incident after a 27-second video went viral on social media. “A team from the Kuala Kurau Fisheries Office was sent to the location this morning to confirm whether the marine mammal carcass is still there or whether the video is an old recording. Elaborating on the discovery of the dolphin carcass, Mohd Ghazali said that based on observations from the video, the marine mammal was estimated to be about two metres long and between seven and nine years old.

items.title: Home minister orders immediate probe into deaths of three cops in Beaufort electric shock tragedy
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — A comprehensive and transparent investigation has been ordered immediately to determine the actual cause of the electric shock tragedy that claimed the lives of three Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel in Beaufort yesterday. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that any weaknesses identified must be addressed immediately, while improvements must also be implemented to ensure that a similar incident does not recur. He also expessed his condolences to the families of Corporal Mohamad Nur Hafiz Ibrahim, Constable Muhammad Raimi Ismarubee and Corporal Chiu Teck Siong.

items.title: ‘If the head is gone, the tail will follow’: Bersatu leaders resign in Terengganu
items.summary: MARANG, Aug 7 — Terengganu Bersatu was left reeling after Datuk Razali Idris announced his resignation as state chief, a post he has held for a decade. “I am only resigning as state chief and division chief, but I remain a party member,” he said. Another top leader, Bersatu Kuala Nerus division chief and deputy speaker of the Terengganu assembly Khazan Che Mat, who is also the party’s deputy state chief, is expected to follow suit.

items.title: Former Chief Justice Mohamed Eusoff Chin dies at 91
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin passed away today at the age of 91. He said a message posted by the late Mohamed Eusoff’s daughter, Zuliana, stated that her father passed away at 1am today. Mohamed Eusoff served as Malaysia’s second Chief Justice from September 1994 to December 2000.

items.title: Ex‑PM Ismail Sabri in IJN, corruption charge postponed to Aug 27
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob will not be charged at the Sessions Court in Kuala Lumpur today, as he is currently warded at the National Heart Institute (IJN). While Ismail Sabri’s case was called up in court this morning, his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad informed the judge that the politician had been admitted to IJN since yesterday. Amer said Ismail Sabri was at the Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission’s (MACC) headquarters yesterday to record his statement, accompanied by his lawyer Ragunath Kesavan.

items.title: Malaysia-Thailand border smuggling drops after illegal jetty crackdown
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 7 — The closure of illegal bases along the Malaysia-Thailand border has disrupted the movement and transit network of smuggling syndicates, thus contributing to a significant decrease in smuggling cases detected in Kelantan. Kelantan Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) director Hanif Yusabra Yusof said the closure of illegal routes has caused syndicates to face difficulties in carrying out smuggling activities as their access and transit routes have been affected. “When access for smuggling is closed, the control of the enforcement authorities becomes better and it helps enforcement operations,” he told Bernama recently.

items.title: Man found dead in Gua Musang cave
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Aug 7 — An elderly man was found dead in a cave near a resort in Kampung Pulai, here, last night. Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Operations commander Che Razak Harun said his department received a call at 9.41pm before 13 members with two engines and two four-wheel drive vehicles were rushed to the location. He said upon arrival at 9.57pm, firefighters found the victim, estimated to be in his 70s, unconscious in the cave.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng slams Reezal’s ‘cordial ties’ claim, says Umno acting as enemy within
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Lim Guan Eng has hit back at Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican over remarks describing ties between Umno and DAP in Penang as “cordial and tension free”. Lim said Reezal’s comments were not only unfriendly but harsh towards supposed allies in the state government. “Can ties between Umno and DAP in the Penang government remain cordial and tension free when Umno behaves like an ‘enemy within’ by making such unwarranted attacks?

items.title: Malaysia condemns Israeli violations at Al-Aqsa, settlement expansion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia condemned the continued violations at Al-Aqsa Mosque and the expansion of Israeli illegal settlements during a ministerial meeting of Arab and Islamic countries on Wednesday. The Ministerial Meeting in Support of Jerusalem and Its Holy Sites was held in Jordan to discuss the escalation in Occupied Jerusalem and to formulate a common position in response. Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry reemphasised that Jerusalem is an integral part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory and strongly rejected any attempt to alter its legal, historical, demographic, and religious status.

items.title: Infant injured as Toyota Alphard and Hilux collide in Seri Kembangan, two adults hurt
items.summary: SERI KEMBANGAN, Aug 7 — A five month old boy suffered facial injuries in a collision involving two multi purpose vehicles (MPVs) and a four wheel drive at Taman Universiti Indah last night. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the emergency call was received at 9.44pm, Harian Metro (HM) reported He said the accident involved a Toyota Alphard and a Toyota Hilux. The five month old boy travelling with them sustained facial injuries,” he said in a statement to HM.

items.title: College student drowns while swimming with friends in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN, Aug 7 — A Kolej Ketengah student in Bandar Al-Muktafi Billah Shah was found drowned after swimming with nine friends at Sungai Loh in Kampung Jongok Batu, Hulu Dungun, near here yesterday. Bandar Al-Muktafi Billah Shah Fire and Rescue Station Operations Commander, Senior Fire Officer I Kamal Suhaimi Abdullah, said the victim, Ahmad Al Hafiz Asri Ahmad, 19, was found by volunteer fire brigade members trapped between rocks about 10 metres from where he was reported missing at 5.20pm. Eight firefighters and three volunteer fire brigade members were involved in the search and rescue operation.

items.title: Bodies of three Beaufort policemen sent to Kota Kinabalu for post-mortems
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The bodies of three police officers who died, believed to have been electrocuted in Beaufort, were yesterday taken to the Forensic Department, Queen Elizabeth Hospital here from Beaufort Hospital early this morning for post-mortem. A Bernama observation at the hospital compound found that the three vans carrying the bodies arrived at 1.10am accompanied by several Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) patrol vehicles from the Beaufort, Papar, Penampang and Kota Kinabalu District Police Headquarters. Beaufort district police chief Supt Champin Piuh when contacted said the bodies would undergo post-mortem and documentation process before being handed over to the next of kin.

items.title: Nurul Izzah steps aside as PKR deputy to pursue studies
items.summary: In a Facebook post yesterday, she said she would remain a PKR member and continue supporting the party’s struggle towards building a better Malaysia. “I will continue to remain a Keadilan (PKR) member, supporting the struggle for a better Malaysia led by the party’s leadership under Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim together with its grassroots,” she said. Nurul Izzah also expressed her appreciation to Anwar and the party leadership for respecting her decision to step down as deputy president.

items.title: High Court quashes RM313.8m tax bill against Daim’s widow Na’imah
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 7 — The High Court here yesterday allowed the judicial review application by Toh Puan Na’imah Abdul Khalid, the wife of former Finance Minister Tun Daim Zainuddin, to quash an additional tax assessment notice amounting to RM313.8 million issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB). Judge Evawani Farisyta Mohammad ruled that the IRB had acted beyond its jurisdiction under the Income Tax Act 1967 when it issued the additional assessment notice dated August 13, 2024, for the 2018 assessment year. She said the Income Tax Act 1967 applied only to income earned in Malaysia and foreign-sourced income remitted into Malaysia, while the assets in dispute were Na’imah’s properties abroad and did not constitute income received in the country.

items.title: Anwar orders full probe into deaths of three Beaufort policemen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent, and prompt investigation into the incident that claimed the lives of three police officers, believed to be due to electrocution in Kampung Weston, Beaufort, Sabah, yesterday. In a Facebook post, Anwar said that the investigation is crucial to identify the cause of the tragic incident and to ensure that corrective measures are taken to prevent similar occurrences from happening again. “I have requested for a comprehensive, transparent, and prompt investigation to be conducted to determine the cause of this tragic incident.

items.title: Three policemen die after suspected electrocution in Beaufort
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — Three policemen were killed, suspected of having been electrocuted along Jalan Weston, Kampung Weston, Beaufort yesterday afternoon. In a statement, the Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said it received a distress call at 5.56pm. “The initial report stated that three victims had been electrocuted along Jalan Weston, Kampung Weston, before the fire brigade was deployed to carry out rescue operations,” the statement read.

items.title: Ismail Sabri expected to face MACC charge at IJN, Sessions Court judge to preside
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob is scheduled to face a charge under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act this morning at the National Heart Institute (IJN). According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the Bera MP’s case will be heard before Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin at the hospital. Ismail’s lawyer Ragunath Kesavan confirmed his client had been admitted to IJN.
